classification.difficultyReason: Derive symbolic winning probabilities from disjoint paths, then follow the explicit subtraction and factorisation instruction to interpret positivity over the given interval.

inlines.text: A biased coin has probability of landing on heads
. Two possible games, involving the biased coin, are offered to Bob.
, he flips the coin two times and wins if he lands on heads at least once.
, he flips the coin three times and wins if he lands on heads at least twice.
Show that the probability of winning Game

answer.short:
$\mathcal{P}(A)=2p-p^2$.

Use the complement of no heads in two flips.
answer.worked:
The complement of winning Game $A$ is getting two tails.

$$\begin{align*}\mathcal{P}(A)&=1-(1-p)^2\\\mathcal{P}(A)&=1-(1-2p+p^2)\\\mathcal{P}(A)&=2p-p^2.\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Show that the probability of winning Game

answer.short:
$\mathcal{P}(B)=3p^2-2p^3$.

Add the three equally likely two-head cases and the all-heads case: $3p^2(1-p)+p^3$.
answer.worked:
Let $H$ and $T$ denote heads and tails. The winning paths are $HHT$, $HTH$, $THH$ and $HHH$. Multiplying along the tree branches gives $p^2(1-p)$ for each two-head path and $p^3$ for $HHH$.

$$\begin{align*}\mathcal{P}(B)&=3p^2(1-p)+p^3\\\mathcal{P}(B)&=3p^2-3p^3+p^3\\\mathcal{P}(B)&=3p^2-2p^3.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored three-flip probability tree supporting the answer-key method. Each H branch has probability p and each T branch has probability 1-p; all eight ordered outcomes are shown.
spec.mathematics: Independent flips; winning paths HHH, HHT, HTH and THH. Their probabilities sum to p^3+3p^2(1-p).
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no tree or path probabilities appear in the student prompt.

inlines.text: and factorising the result, determine which game Bob should pick.

answer.short:
Bob should pick Game $A$ for every $0<p<1$.

$\mathcal{P}(A)-\mathcal{P}(B)=2p(p-1)^2>0$ throughout the stated interval.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\mathcal{P}(A)-\mathcal{P}(B)&=(2p-p^2)-(3p^2-2p^3)\\\mathcal{P}(A)-\mathcal{P}(B)&=2p-4p^2+2p^3\\\mathcal{P}(A)-\mathcal{P}(B)&=2p(1-2p+p^2)\\\mathcal{P}(A)-\mathcal{P}(B)&=2p(p-1)^2.\end{align*}$$

Since $0<p<1$, both $2p$ and $(p-1)^2$ are positive. Hence $\mathcal{P}(A)>\mathcal{P}(B)$, so Bob should pick Game $A$.
